original_question: What extremely rare congenital disorder is caused by a mutation in the gene encoding the G protein-activated inward rectifier potassium channel 2?
key_entities: G protein-activated inward rectifier potassium channel 2

final_qi.question: What extremely rare congenital disorder is caused by a mutation in the gene encoding the G protein-activated inward rectifier potassium channel 2?
final_qi.long_answer: Keppen-Lubinsky syndrome is an extremely rare congenital disorder characterized by severe congenital lipodystrophy, distinctive facial features, growth and developmental delay, and brain anomalies. It is caused by de novo gain-of-function mutations in the KCNJ6 gene, which encodes the G protein-activated inward rectifier potassium channel 2 (GIRK2). Disruption of GIRK2 channel activity alters neuronal and metabolic signaling, producing the clinical features of the syndrome.
